basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 12:17 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 158. Et erit semen tuum sicut stellae coeli et sicut arena quae est in littore'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 158. Et erit semen tuum sicut stellae coeli et sicut arena quae est in littore maris (Gen. XII, 17). Qui significati sunt in stellis, et qui in arena?-- Resp. In stellis [coeli] pauciores firmioresque [et] clariores intelliguntur; in arena autem maritimi littoris, magna multitudo infirmorum atque carnalium.
